summary: Phase 2 realtime sync channel (WS /api/ws/sync) validated end-to-end. Backend: 7/7 new tests pass (initial payload with data+h equal to HTTP /sync digest; bad token rejected; friend request push 0.14-0.16s and decline push ~0.2s; mm_found pushed ~0.6-1.3s after 4th join (bounded by matchmaking loop tick) + status found same game_id + current_game sync push; mm_update on duo decline 0.13s; ping->pong + last_active updated + tester1 counted online for tester2; safety refresh after ~11.8s with counters only (no data when unchanged)). Regression suites iter32 sync/ratelimit, friends, iter30 duo, admin stats: 32/32 pass. Frontend (844x390): exactly ONE /api/ws/sync WS after login, ZERO HTTP /api/sync over 22s idle on Home (only 1 initial /sync at login), online count visible; friend request from tester2 shows bell+menu badge instantly with zero HTTP calls and clears instantly on decline; forced WS drop -> immediate HTTP /sync catch-up then reconnect exactly 3.0s later and polling stops again. Matchmaking 'Jouer en ligne > Rapide': browser navigated to /game/{id} 2.02s after the 4th scripted player joined (mm_found frame at +1.01s, status check at +1.09s, +0.7s intentional animation delay). No deprecated Expo packages touched in this scope.

minor.issue: websocket.close(4001) is called BEFORE accept(), so Starlette rejects the handshake with HTTP 403 — clients never see close code 4001 (browser gets 1006). Same pattern as /ws/game. Harmless (client falls back + retries every 20s) but if a 4001 code is wanted for 'session expired -> logout' logic, accept() first then close(4001).

Inviter only gets a generic sync push, not an mm_update event, so the inviter's waiting screen goes duo_pending -> waiting only on its next status poll (<=5s). Consider push_event(mm_update) to the inviter on online duo accept for consistency with decline.

integration_issues.issue: checkStatus() returns early when a status poll is already in flight (`checking` flag). If mm_found arrives while a poll that started before the match formed is in flight, the signal is dropped and navigation waits for the next poll (up to ~5s). Fix: set a 'recheck' flag when skipped and re-run checkStatus once the in-flight one finishes. Reference: /app/frontend/app/matchmaking.tsx:105-117

action_items: (Optional) matchmaking.tsx: don't drop mmSignal when a status check is in flight — queue a re-check.
(Optional) ws_sync: accept() before close(4001) if the client should distinguish invalid token from network errors.
(Optional) push mm_update to the inviter on online duo accept.
critical_code_review_comments: sync_channel push is per-process (in-memory _conns); fine with --workers 1. With multiple workers, mm_found from the matchmaking loop running in another process is NOT pushed as an event — only covered by the 12s refresher's current_game data (client navigates only via its own status poll). Keep in mind if scaling workers.

Each open sync socket runs a 12s refresher doing ~4 Mongo queries (count users, scan mm_queue up to 200, notifications payload, current game) — lighter than 7s HTTP polling but scales linearly with connections; consider a shared global counters tick if user count grows.
uvicorn --reload watches /app/backend including tests/: creating/editing test files reloads the backend and drops all sync/game sockets (dev-only side effect, observed in logs).
